analysis.title: Expeditors Int'l of Washington (EXPD): 3Q26 EPS Ahead on Air Strength Continuance; Ocean Supply Acceleration in 2027 Could Weigh on Rates
key_insights: EXPD (Sell) reported 3Q26 operating EPS of $2.65 vs $2.20 GS estimate and $2.21 Visible Alpha consensus, a 20% beat vs GS and 20% vs consensus.
The beat came from Air: gross air revenue was 16% above GSe on higher volume and revenue per kilo, and air net revenue was 16% above GSe.
EBIT of about $445M was 18% above GSe on slightly lower opex. EBIT was 36.7% of net revenue vs 33% GSe, above the 30% level GS uses to judge health.
Net revenue of about $1,214M was 6% above GSe. Net revenue margin of 29.5% was 50bps below the 30.1% GS forecast.
Air net revenue margin was 24.3%, in line with GSe. Air rates rose 38% y/y vs GSe +20%, and air kilo growth was 13%.
Ocean net revenue was 4% below GSe. Ocean rates rose 41% on 7% volume growth, with net revenue margin in line.
Air and ocean volume growth was +13%/+7% y/y in 3Q26, vs +14%/0% in 2Q26 and GS forecasts of +10%/+3%.
Customs brokerage net revenue beat GSe by 4% on 8% higher total revenue. Net revenue margin of 40.9% was below GSe 42.5% and 2Q26's 42.1%.
Ocean volume growth accelerated through the quarter: +5% in July, +5% in August, +12% in September. Air accelerated from +8% to +13% to +19% over the same months.

Air demand was driven by South Asia, hyperscalers and an e-commerce recovery on Asia-to-US lanes lapping de minimis impacts. Capacity is constrained by limited fleet expansion and aircraft delivery delays.
Management cited hyperscaler demand for goods movement and favorable e-commerce trends out of North Asia. GS sees a possible positive read-through to parcel carriers UPS and FDX.
GS expects meaningful ocean supply growth in 2H27 that could offset air tailwinds, and points to its European ocean analyst's recent downgrade of MAERSK.
Strong 2026 net revenue and EPS growth sets up difficult 2027 comparisons.
GS raised FY26/27/28 EPS to $8.55/$8.80/$9.50 from $7.90/$8.35/$8.95. The 12-month price target rose to $185 from $180, based on about 20.0x P/E (from 21.0x) on Q5-Q8 EPS of $9.30.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $185 from $180 on higher EPS estimates, with the P/E multiple cut to about 20.0x from 21.0x because 2026 may be the peak of net revenue growth. The stock closed at $200.56, 7.8% above the target.

sector_views.rationale: Air capacity is tight and rates are elevated, but ocean supply growth in 2H27 could offset the air tailwinds.

earnings_insights: EXPD 3Q26 reported operating EPS $2.65 (reported 11/3) vs GS estimate $2.20 and Visible Alpha consensus $2.21.
3Q26 net revenue $1,213.7M reported vs GS estimate $1,148.9M and consensus $1,117.7M. Total revenue $4,107.6M vs GS $3,821.9M and consensus $3,618.2M.
3Q26 operating income $445.4M reported vs GS estimate $378.8M and consensus $379.3M. Operating income as a percent of net revenue was 36.7% vs GS 33.0% and consensus 33.9%.
3Q26 tax rate was 23.1% vs GS estimate 26.0%, which added to the net income beat.
GS FY EPS estimates (new vs old): 2026E $8.55 vs $7.90, 2027E $8.80 vs $8.35, 2028E $9.50 vs $8.95. GS quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26E $2.12, 1Q27E $1.99, 2Q27E $2.16.
risk_factors: Ocean supply influx in 2H27 could pressure rates and offset air strength.
2026 may be the peak of net revenue growth, with difficult 2027 comparisons.

Upside risks to the Sell thesis: restocking-driven consumer volume, continued customs brokerage demand, contract pricing holding firmer than expected, the asset-light model proving more resilient in a slowdown, and a Red Sea ceasefire that ends and tightens capacity.
geopolitical: Trade and geopolitical uncertainty persists. The duration of the Middle East conflict could affect air prices through fuel costs and capacity.
The report names the unknown duration of the Red Sea conflict ceasefire as an upside risk, since it could tighten capacity and raise rates.

tension_points.theme: EXPD air strength vs 2027 ocean supply
tension_points.bull_case: Tight air capacity, hyperscaler demand and e-commerce recovery drove a 20% EPS beat and higher estimates, with air volume growth accelerating to +19% in September.
tension_points.bear_case: Strong 2026 comparisons plus meaningful ocean supply growth in 2H27 could slow net revenue growth and pressure rates, which is why GS cut its target multiple to 20.0x.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Red Sea ceasefire that ends and tightens capacity and lifts rates would work against the bearish view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Meaningful ocean supply growth in 2H27 could offset the positive tailwinds in air.
theme_stances.evidence: we anticipate an influx of ocean supply in 2H27
